title: Disk Evolution Study Through Imaging of Nearby Young Stars (DESTINYS): PDS 111, an old T Tauri star with a young-looking disk
question: Reassess the age of the G-type T Tauri star PDS 111 and measure its disk properties (dust, gas, scattered light) to see how it fits disk evolution and the Peter Pan disk scenario

evidence.quote: is known to be in the foreground of the Orion star-forming region at a distance of 158 pc

evidence.quote: we selected the mean V-band measurement of the ASAS-SN survey with 279 measurements over a period of five years in order to account for the variations

recipe.method: Run the ALMA scriptforPI, flag +-20 km/s around 12CO, build a pseudo-continuum averaged to 125 MHz and 6 s, self-calibrate on the continuum (4 phase then amplitude), apply tables to the 12CO window
key_parameters: phase solution intervals inf, 40s, 18s, 6s; amplitude 6s; spws and scans combined
imaging for self-calibration with Briggs robust 0.5

recipe.goal: Image continuum and 12CO with JvM correction
recipe.method: Continuum imaged with robust -0.5; 12CO with robust 0.0 and no taper; both cleaned to 4 sigma then JvM-corrected

recipe.goal: Check optical depth and derive dust mass
recipe.method: Compute tau at the continuum peak from I = B(Td)(1 - exp(-tau)); if optically thin, M_dust = d^2 F_nu / (kappa_nu B_nu(T))
assumptions: dust temperature of 20 K for the optical depth
optically thin emission; distance to the source d

recipe.goal: Fit the continuum visibilities with a parametric model
recipe.method: Four-component brightness model (central Gaussian, two ring Gaussians, azimuthal Gaussian asymmetry) Fourier transformed with galario and sampled with zeus MCMC
key_parameters: model images with 4 mas pixels and 2048 pixel image size
n_walk = 136 (eight times the number of parameters), 5000 burn-in steps and 6000 sampling steps per walker

recipe.goal: Measure radial extent of dust, gas and scattered light
recipe.method: Deproject and azimuthally average the ALMA images; take the radius enclosing 90% of the emission; SPHERE shown as radial cuts along the major axis

recipe.goal: Derive stellar mass from 12CO Keplerian rotation
recipe.method: Fit the Keplerian rotation pattern of 12CO with eddy using a simple disk model
key_parameters: inclination fixed to the continuum value

recipe.method: Fit Kurucz models to the 402-430 nm X-shooter spectrum for Teff, log g, v sin i; fit SED for luminosity and radius; place the star on Siess et al. tracks in the HRD
key_parameters: Kurucz grid: Teff 5500-6500 K step 100 K, log g 4.0-4.5 step 0.1, v sin i 20-50 km/s step 1
R_V fixed to 3.1 in the SED fit; distance and Teff fixed
assumptions: Gaia DR3 distance (RUWE 2.6 discussed and judged not to invalidate it)

recipe.goal: Reduce SPHERE data and trace the disk surface
recipe.method: IRDAP polarimetric differential imaging and ADI (PCA), then trace individual rings by eye as ellipses on polarized, high-pass filtered and AIDA-deconvolved images to get aspect ratios
key_parameters: ADI with 4 principal components; optimization annuli 10-30, 30-100, 100-512 pixels
ring inclination and PA fixed to the ALMA values

recipe.goal: Measure accretion rate and spectral variability
recipe.method: EW of lines after Kurucz model subtraction converted to line luminosity and accretion rate with Alcala et al. relations; temporal variance spectrum for variability
key_parameters: 95% level used for a significant TVS detection
assumptions: inner radius of 5 R_star for the accretion rate
